questions.question: Dr. Meknassi, the sole partner of a single-member LLC, dies suddenly. According to the 2024 amendments to Law 5-96, what must his heirs do?
options: Automatically dissolve the company within 30 days
Request the court to appoint a representative within 60 days
Transfer the shares without any formality
Sell the practice to a colleague within 15 days
questions.explanation: The 2024 amendments (Laws 44.24 and 45.24) specify that in the event of death of the sole partner, an heir may request the president of the court to appoint a representative to convene a general meeting within 60 days.

questions.question: Dr. Zemmouri is the manager of a standard LLC. He wishes to borrow from his own company. According to Article 66 of Law 5-96, is this permitted?
options: Yes, if the partners' meeting authorizes it
No, the prohibition is absolute and extends to relatives
Yes, if it is a loan of 50,000 DH maximum
No, but his spouse can do it on his behalf
questions.explanation: Article 66 prohibits managers and partners who are natural persons from borrowing from the company, in any form whatsoever. This prohibition also applies to spouses, parents, and in-laws up to the second degree.

questions.question: Dr. Meknassi is the manager of an LLC. He wishes to commit the company to a 5-year lease. A statutory clause requires him to obtain the partners' agreement for any contract exceeding 2 years. What happens if he signs anyway?
options: The contract is null and void
The manager incurs civil liability towards the partners
The company is automatically dissolved
The contract becomes the manager's personal contract
questions.explanation: According to Article 8 of Law 5-96, in the event of violation of a statutory limitation, the manager incurs civil liability towards the partners. Statutory clauses limiting the powers of managers are unenforceable against third parties.

questions.question: Dr. Zemmouri is the sole partner of a single-member LLC. In the event of death, an heir requests the appointment of a representative. What is the time limit for this procedure?
options: 30 days from death
60 days from death
90 days from death
6 months from death
questions.explanation: The 2024 amendment to Article 85 of Law 5-96 provides a period of 60 days from the date of death to request the appointment of a representative.

questions.question: Dr. Meknassi, as a natural person, wishes to open a bank account for his practice. According to Article 18 of the Commercial Code, what must he do?
options: Use his personal account to simplify management
Open a separate professional account
Open a joint account with his spouse
No obligation, he can operate in cash
questions.explanation: Article 18 of the Commercial Code requires any merchant to open a professional bank account for their business needs.

questions.question: Dr. Zemmouri has an LLC. According to Article 63 of Law 5-96, what are the manager's powers towards third parties?
options: He can only commit the company for acts expressly authorized by the articles
He commits the company through acts falling within the corporate purpose
He must obtain the agreement of all partners for each act
He can only commit the company for acts under 100,000 DH
questions.explanation: According to Article 63, the manager commits the company through acts falling within the corporate purpose. Statutory clauses limiting his powers are unenforceable against third parties.

questions.question: Dr. Meknassi is the manager of an LLC with his colleague. One of them opposes a contract before it is concluded. According to Law 5-96, is this opposition enforceable against third parties?
options: Yes, if the opposition is notified in writing
No, the opposition has no effect on third parties
Yes, if the third party had knowledge of it
No, unless the manager is the majority partner
questions.explanation: In the case of multiple managers, opposition by one manager to acts of another has no effect on third parties, unless it is established that they had knowledge of it.

questions.question: Dr. Zemmouri, as a natural person, is subject to the Commercial Code. In the event of financial difficulties, what is the main risk?
options: Automatic dissolution of his practice
Seizure of his personal assets by creditors
Removal from the Order's register
A 5-year ban from practicing
questions.explanation: As a natural person, there is no distinction between professional and personal assets. Creditors can seize all the dentist's assets, including personal ones.

questions.question: Dr. Meknassi, the sole partner of a single-member LLC, dies. His heirs do nothing for 60 days. What is the consequence provided by law?
options: The company is automatically dissolved
The company continues without change
Dissolution of the company is the possible sanction for inaction
The shares are attributed to the surviving spouse
questions.explanation: The proposed amendment does not expressly provide for the sanction of inaction by heirs within the 60-day period, but dissolution of the company is the possible consequence.

questions.question: According to Article 6 of the Commercial Code, is a dental surgeon a merchant in the commercial sense of the term?
options: Yes, because he carries out a lucrative activity
No, because dentists are not covered by Article 6
Yes, because he is subject to professional tax
No, because he does not buy to resell in the same state
questions.explanation: Article 6 of the Commercial Code defines commercial acts by nature. The activity of a dentist, as a liberal healthcare profession, is not covered. The dentist is not a merchant in the commercial sense, but is subject to the Commercial Code for formal obligations.

questions.question: Dr. Zemmouri has a standard LLC with 3 partners. One partner wishes to transfer his shares to a colleague. According to Law 5-96, what is the applicable rule?
options: Transfer is free without any conditions
Transfer is subject to partners' approval if the articles provide for it
Transfer is prohibited during the first 5 years
Transfer is automatic without formalities
questions.explanation: Law 5-96 allows partners to include approval clauses in the articles for the transfer of shares. Freedom of transfer is not absolute in an LLC.

questions.question: Dr. Meknassi, as a natural person, has a turnover of 250,000 DH. According to the GTC, which tax regime applies to him?
options: The Actual Net Income regime (RNR)
The Simplified Net Income regime (RNS)
The Single Professional Contribution regime (CPU)
The flat-rate regime
questions.explanation: For liberal professions, RNS applies to natural persons whose turnover is between 250,000 and 500,000 DH.

questions.question: Dr. Zemmouri, the sole partner of a single-member LLC, wishes to hire his son. According to good governance rules, what must he check?
options: Nothing, the single-member LLC offers total freedom of hiring
Compliance with the Labor Code and conflict of interest rules
Obligation to declare the hiring to the Order of Dentists
Prior authorization from the commercial court
questions.explanation: Even in a single-member LLC, hiring a relative must comply with the Labor Code and avoid any conflict of interest, particularly regarding salary setting.

questions.question: Dr. Meknassi, manager of an LLC, wishes to create a branch. According to Law 5-96, what is the rule?
options: He can do it freely without authorization
He must obtain a collective decision from the partners
He must request court authorization
Creating a branch is prohibited in an LLC
questions.explanation: The manager of an LLC has the broadest powers to act on behalf of the company. Creating a branch is an ordinary management act within his powers.

questions.question: Dr. Zemmouri, as a natural person, is taxed under the BNC regime. Can he deduct expenses related to his personal car?
options: Yes, fully if used for the practice
Only the duly justified professional portion
No, car expenses are never deductible
Yes, if the vehicle is in his name
questions.explanation: Under BNC, only expenses incurred for professional activity are deductible. The personal portion must be distinguished from the professional portion.

questions.question: Dr. Meknassi, a partner in an LLC, wishes to receive remuneration. According to Law 5-96, how is it determined?
options: It is freely set by the manager
It is set by an ordinary collective decision of the partners
It is set by ministerial order
It is definitively set by the articles
questions.explanation: Managers may receive remuneration, the terms of which are determined by an ordinary collective decision of the partners.

questions.question: Is Dr. Zemmouri, as a natural person, subject to corporate income tax (CIT)?
options: Yes, like any liberal professional
No, he is subject to personal income tax (PIT)
Yes, if he makes a profit exceeding 200,000 DH
No, dentists are exempt from tax
questions.explanation: Natural persons practicing as sole proprietors are subject to personal income tax (PIT), BNC category. CIT only concerns legal entities.

questions.question: Dr. Meknassi, the sole partner of a single-member LLC, dies. His heirs wish to continue the activity. According to amended Law 5-96, what must they do?
options: Nothing, they automatically take over management
Request the court to appoint a representative to convene a general meeting
Create a new company within 30 days
Sell the shares to a colleague within 15 days
questions.explanation: The 2024 amendments to Article 85 allow heirs or beneficiaries to request the president of the competent court to appoint a representative to hold a general meeting and update the articles.

questions.question: Dr. Zemmouri, manager of an LLC, wants to buy a building. According to Law 5-96, does this type of transaction require partners' approval?
options: Yes, if the articles provide for it
No, the manager has all powers
Yes, it is a mandatory extraordinary decision
No, buying a building is prohibited in an LLC
questions.explanation: The manager has the broadest powers to act in all circumstances on behalf of the company. However, the articles may limit these powers by requiring prior approval of partners for certain operations.

questions.question: Dr. Meknassi, as a natural person, has a turnover of 800,000 DH. What is the rate of his Minimum Contribution?
questions.explanation: For natural persons subject to PIT, the CM is calculated at a rate of 6% of turnover.

questions.question: According to the Code of Ethics, can Dr. Zemmouri advertise his practice using commercial discounts?
options: Yes, to attract new patients
No, commercial advertising is prohibited
Yes, if approved by the Order
No, but he can post offers on social media
questions.explanation: The Code of Ethics prohibits any commercial advertising. The dentist cannot engage in mercantile practices such as loyalty discounts.

questions.question: Dr. Meknassi is the manager of an LLC. According to Article 66 of Law 5-96, can he have the company guarantee a personal loan?
options: Yes, if the partners agree
No, this prohibition is absolute
Yes, for an amount under 50,000 DH
Yes, if the loan is for the practice
questions.explanation: Article 66 prohibits managers from having the company guarantee or endorse their commitments to third parties, regardless of the amount.

questions.question: Dr. Zemmouri, as a natural person, has a tax deficit of 50,000 DH. Under the RNR regime, over how many years can he carry it forward?
options: 2 years
3 years
4 years
5 years
questions.explanation: Under the RNR regime, the deficit can be carried forward against profits of the following four years.

questions.question: Dr. Meknassi, the sole partner of a single-member LLC, wishes to dissolve his company. According to Law 5-96, what is the procedure?
options: He can do so by a simple personal decision
He must convene an extraordinary general meeting
He must obtain court approval
He must wait for the end of the current financial year
questions.explanation: The sole partner exercises the powers conferred on all partners. He can therefore decide alone on the dissolution of the company, without having to convene a meeting.

questions.question: Dr. Zemmouri, as a natural person, wishes to create an LLC with 3 colleagues. What is the current minimum capital requirement?
options: 1 Dirham
questions.explanation: Since Law 24-10, the share capital is freely set by the partners. A symbolic capital of 1 Dirham is possible.
